name: exp-adventure
start: A live-action film still, 1930s pulp adventure, full-frame 16:9 with no letterbox bars. Inside a torch-lit ancient stone temple chamber: carved sandstone walls, a low stone pedestal in the centre holding a small jade mask, dust in the air, two burning wall torches, a dark doorway at the back. In the foreground stands an adventurer: an original fictional character who does not resemble any real actor. A Black man in his early thirties, deep brown skin, close-cropped hair, a short neat beard, a broad friendly face, wearing a weathered tan fedora, a dusty olive canvas field jacket over a cream shirt, and a leather satchel across his chest. He faces the pedestal from a few steps away, seen from a fixed wide camera at eye height. Warm torchlight, deep shadows, light film grain. No text.
clips: Fixed wide camera, no camera movement. The adventurer walks up to the pedestal, studies the jade mask for a moment, then carefully lifts it off the pedestal with both hands. The pedestal sinks a few inches with a grinding sound and dust trickles from the ceiling. He looks up, alarmed, and slips the mask into his satchel.

The chamber begins to shake. Dust and small stones fall from the ceiling, the torches flicker. The adventurer turns and runs toward the dark doorway at the back of the chamber, hat held on with one hand, as a large stone block drops from above and crashes behind him. Camera holds steady.

The adventurer sprints out of the dark doorway into bright jungle daylight, dives forward and rolls through the dirt as the stone door slams shut behind him. He gets to his feet, dusts off his fedora, puts it back on, opens his satchel and looks at the jade mask with a tired grin. Camera holds steady.
